This bill would keep funding grants that support pay for early childhood education and care workers.
It would amend the Wage Justice for Early Childhood Education and Care Workers (Special Account) Act to extend the special account's operation and the wage increase program.
The extension would run to 30 June 2028 and also aims to improve safety and quality in the sector.
The bill would extend the special account's funding for worker pay until 30 June 2028.
It would extend the Act's sunset provision because payments are made in arrears.
It would ensure the next phase of the wage program supports safe and quality early childhood education and care.

Senator Waters [explained that](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2026-03-25.27.1): > *This amendment would require the government to actually respond to the recommendations of the commissioner that this bill is establishing as an independent statutory position. The bill allows the commissioner to seek information from governments to inform her reports and recommendations, but there is nothing in the bill to compel the government to actually respond to those recommendations. I think that is tragic and I think it is very easily fixed. The optimist in me thought it was an oversight; however, it seems to be by design, and I think that is heartbreaking. This bill would create a new parliamentary committee to oversee Australia's defence agencies.
The committee would have up to 13 members and could request information, documents, and briefings, but would be restricted from publicly disclosing sensitive information without ministerial approval.
The bill includes criminal offences for unauthorised use or disclosure of protected information by committee members, their staff, and other authorised parliamentarians.
Creates the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Defence within the Defence Act 1903.
Gives the committee power to review, monitor, and report on Australian defence agencies, excluding certain intelligence organisations.
Imposes restrictions on public proceedings and disclosure of protected information, with ministerial certificates overriding disclosure requirements.
Establishes criminal offences for unauthorised use or disclosure of protected information.

Australian defence agencies, including the Australian Defence Force, Department of Defence, and Department of Veterans' Affairs, as well as committee members, their staff, and other authorised parliamentarians.

Moved the Crimes Amendment (Prohibiting the Strip Searching of Children) Bill 2026 for second reading, arguing that strip searching children is ineffective, traumatising, degrading and inconsistent with children's rights. The explanatory memorandum was tabled, leave was granted to incorporate the speech in Hansard, and debate was adjourned.
Crimes Amendment (Prohibiting Shackling During Childbirth) Bill 2026

Moved the Crimes Amendment (Prohibiting Shackling During Childbirth) Bill 2026 for second reading, arguing that shackling during childbirth is unnecessary, dangerous, medically harmful, degrading and inconsistent with human rights obligations. The explanatory memorandum was tabled, leave was granted to incorporate the speech in Hansard, and debate was adjourned.
